def describe_Cols(data_map):
    for key, df in data_map.items():
        print(f"Dataframe: {key}")
        print(f"Shape: {df.shape}")
        print(f"Columns: {df.columns.tolist()}")    
        for col in df.columns:
            if df[col].isna().sum() > 0:
                print(f"Column '{col}' has {df[col].isna().sum()} missing values.")
        print("")

# Deriving provider gender from first names
print("Deriving gender for providers from first names...")

# Initialize the gender detector 
gender_detector = gender.Detector()

def guess_gender(name):
    if pd.isna(name):
        return 'unknown'
    # Use 'unknown' as default, specify country if possible (e.g., 'usa')
    guessed = gender_detector.get_gender(str(name).split()[0]) # Use only the first word
    if guessed in ['male', 'mostly_male']:
        return 'male'
    elif guessed in ['female', 'mostly_female']:
        return 'female'
    else: # andy, unknown
        return 'unknown'
    
# Apply the function to the 'first_name' column of your provider_df

provider_df['derived_gender'] = provider_df['first_name'].apply(guess_gender)
# print(provider_df[['provider_id', 'first_name', 'derived_gender']].head())

print("Provider gender derivation complete.")

# --- 1. Language Data Prep Function ---
def find_additional_languages(lang_list):
    """Processes a list of languages to find non-English or 'None'."""
    # Handle bad data (like NaN or float) just in case
    if not isinstance(lang_list, list):
        return ['Unknown'] 
        
    # Filter out 'English' (and any extra whitespace)
    filtered = [lang.strip() for lang in lang_list if lang.strip() != 'English']
    
    # If the list is now empty, they were English-only
    if not filtered:
        return ['None (English Only)']
    else:
        return filtered

# --- 2. Prepare Language Data *Before* Plotting ---
try:
    languages_col = provider_df['languages_spoken'].fillna('Unknown')
    language_lists = languages_col.str.split('; ')
    additional_languages = language_lists.apply(find_additional_languages)
    
    # Explode the lists into new rows
    final_languages = additional_languages.explode()
    
    # Filter out any 'Unknown' placeholders
    final_languages = final_languages[final_languages != 'Unknown']
    
    # Get order for the new plot
    language_plot_order = final_languages.value_counts().index

except KeyError:
    print("Error: 'languages_spoken' column not found. Can't create language plot.")
    # Exit or handle as needed
except AttributeError:
    print("Error: 'languages_spoken' column has non-string data. Can't process.")
    # Exit or handle as needed


# --- 3. Setup Plotting Variables ---
categorical_columns = [
    'specialty',
    'provider_race',
    'provider_ethnicity',
    'derived_gender',
    'additional_languages'  # <-- Added placeholder for our new plot
]


palettes = [
    "viridis", "plasma", "inferno", "magma",
    "cividis", "rocket", "mako", "crest"
]

# This will now correctly calculate 3 rows ( (5+1)//2 )
rows = len(categorical_columns)//2 + (1 if len(categorical_columns)%2!=0 else 0)

sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# Increased height for 3 rows
fig, axes = plt.subplots(rows, 2, figsize=(18, 24)) 
fig.suptitle('Distributions of Categorical Variables in Provider dataset', fontsize=16)

i = 0
for ax, col in zip(axes.flatten(), categorical_columns):
    
    # --- 4. Main Plotting Logic (if/else) ---
    
    if col == 'additional_languages':
        # --- SPECIAL PLOT for Languages ---
        sns.countplot(
            x=final_languages, # Use prepared data
            order=language_plot_order,
            ax=ax,
            palette=palettes[i % len(palettes)],
            hue=final_languages, # Use prepared data
            legend=False
        )
        ax.set_title('Distribution of Additional Languages', fontsize=16)
        ax.set_xlabel('Language (or "None" for English Only)', fontsize=14)
    
    else:
        # --- REGULAR PLOT for other columns ---
        sns.countplot(
            data=provider_df, 
            x=col, 
            order=provider_df[col].value_counts().index, 
            ax=ax,
            palette=palettes[i % len(palettes)],
            hue=col,
            legend=False
        )
        ax.set_title(f'Distribution of {col}',fontsize=16)
        ax.set_xlabel(col, fontsize=14)
    
    # --- 5. Common Formatting for ALL subplots ---
    i += 1
    ax.set_ylabel('Count', fontsize=12)
    ax.tick_params(axis='x', labelsize=12) # No rotation=0 here

    # Add bar labels
    for c in ax.containers:
        ax.bar_label(c)

    # --- 6. Text Wrapping & Rotation Logic ---
    wrap_width = 15
    ticks = ax.get_xticks()
    labels = [label.get_text() for label in ax.get_xticklabels()]
    wrapped_labels = [textwrap.fill(label, width=wrap_width) for label in labels]
    
    ax.set_xticks(ticks)
    
    # Apply rotation conditionally
    if col == 'specialty':
        ax.set_xticklabels(wrapped_labels, rotation=90, ha='right')
    elif col == 'additional_languages':
         ax.set_xticklabels(wrapped_labels, rotation=45, ha='right')
    else:
        ax.set_xticklabels(wrapped_labels) # Default (no rotation)
    # ---

# --- 7. Final Cleanup ---
# This will now correctly turn off the 6th subplot
if len(categorical_columns) % 2 != 0:
    axes.flatten()[-1].set_visible(False)

plt.tight_layout(w_pad=3, h_pad=4, rect=[0, 0.03, 1, 0.97]) # Increased h_pad
plt.show()

sns.boxplot(data=encounter_df, x='language_match', y='patient_satisfaction', order=[False, True])
plt.title('Patient Satisfaction by Language Match')
plt.xticks([False, True], ['No Match', 'Match'])

# Box plot for language_match vs. treatment_adherence
plt.subplot(1, 2, 2)
sns.boxplot(data=encounter_df, x='language_match', y='treatment_adherence', order=[False, True])
plt.title('Treatment Adherence by Language Match')
plt.xticks([False, True], ['No Match', 'Match'])

plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.03, 1, 0.95])
plt.show()


plt.figure(figsize=(14, 12))

subplot_num=master_df['cultural_preferences'].nunique()

    subset = master_df[master_df['cultural_preferences'] == pref]

    plt.title(f'Preference: {pref}')
    plt.xticks([False, True], ['No Match', 'Match'])

plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.03, 1, 0.95])
plt.show()
